frozen_design.name: D native upper fixed cap probe
frozen_design.question: Does one native-upper fixed cap explain the remaining opportunity before any dynamic controller is developed?
frozen_design.reason: mixed01: all160pass bothcaps,2048U+3.56-3.62%,maxgap<46ms. Native total token limit4096 and max prompt3513 leave a larger legal fixed action.
frozen_design.decision: First require actual execution differences. One fixed cap is provisionally sufficient for the primary objective if its fulljointgoodput improves>=3% in both reversedpairs, allrequestscomplete, rawthroughputdoesnotdecrease, and TTFT/flow/maxgap p95 do not worsen>5%, with noadded100msgapfailures. Otherwise report the completefixedfrontier and whether tradeoff signs repeat; noisy/mixed signs are inconclusive. Only a reproducible tradeoff plus observable state variation warrants count/closest-dynamic comparisons and a new signal. No controller or intermediate-cap grid; same gates retained. All qualification changes reported.
frozen_design.execution: Unmodified parent run_confirmation.py/launch.sh. fixed4096 remains a pure prefill cap; native total4096 and all native allocation/order limits can reduce actualP. Existing assert checks all native decoders served; preserve any failure.

scope: Two reversed pairs on one fresh development arrival, not statistical confirmation. All requests and full elapsed retained; fixed prompt/output counts are not content, routing, computation or quality equivalence. No per-window oracle or controller claim. Mixed signs remain inconclusive; a missing uniform winner alone is not evidence for dynamics.
